Q: What is `kern.num_files` in `sysctl`? A:

Is this actually the count of system-wide open FD?

It has been reported so. Examples:

  • https://apple.stackexchange.com/a/312014
  • https://lucaberton.com/blog/macos-enfile-error-too-many-open-files-fix/.

However ...

Where can I find any spec for this?

MacOS features a relatively large number of substantially undocumented sysctls, and this one is among them. You already know that although it is listed by man sysctl, no description is provided there. Additionally, the description printed by sysctl -d kern.num_files is empty. And I find no spec for this sysctl among Apple's developer docs. Furthermore, this is an Apple invention, not among the sysctls that MacOS inherited from BSD, so there is not even BSD documentation to fall back on.

If you want some kind of official confirmation then your best bet is probably to study the MacOS source, but the unofficial attestations (not limited to the above) seem clear and consistent enough that I would probably rely on them, myself.

Q: Parse a log file line containing square bracketed expressions A:

First, you want the info between the first set of brackets, but as those are special chars for regex we escape them: [(.*?)] -> \[(.*?)\]

$logLine = "[2017-12-23 19:15:59:634187] [INFO] User SIMDesign successfully logged in."
            ^--------------------------^

Then the second brackets, same logic:[(.*?)] -> \[(.*?)\]

$logLine = "[2017-12-23 19:15:59:634187] [INFO] User SIMDesign successfully logged in."
                                         ^----^

And 'the rest till the end' is (.*)$

$logLine = "[2017-12-23 19:15:59:634187] [INFO] User SIMDesign successfully logged in."
                                                ^------------------------------------^

With spaces(\s) between them: \[(.*?)\]\s\[(.*?)\]\s(.*)$, with a neat little demo here

I like the answer I wrote above more, but the preg_split page also documents a few flags you can pass along with preg_split(), one being the following. The reason I'm not a fan is because your 'hiding' the problem instead of fixing it.

PREG_SPLIT_NO_EMPTY
If this flag is set, only non-empty pieces will be returned by preg_split().

Q: Reveal file in tree with NerdTree A:

I have the following workflow with NERDTree:

  • it opens with VIM (regardless if opening a file or not);
  • I use <leader>nc to close all opened NERDTree;
  • I use <leader>no to open NERDTree highlighting current file opened, backing focus to the buffer (it does no work with a empty buffer);
  • when opening a new buffer, also open NERDTree but only if it is already opened.

So it looks like a single panel during the session and is synchronized with the opened buffer. To achieve that I use the following instructions:

" ===== Mappings

map <leader>no  :NERDTreeFind<cr> :wincmd w<cr>
map <leader>nc  :tabdo NERDTreeClose<cr>

" ===== Helper function

function! OpenNERDTreeIfExists()
    if getcmdwintype() != '' || bufname('%') =~# 'NERD_tree'
        return
    endif

    " Check if NERDTree is open in any tab
    for l:tab in range(1, tabpagenr('$'))
        for l:buf in tabpagebuflist(l:tab)
            if bufname(l:buf) =~# 'NERD_tree'
                silent NERDTreeMirror
                silent NERDTreeFind
                return
            endif
        endfor
    endfor
endfunction

" ===== Auto commands

autocmd VimEnter * NERDTree " Start NERDTree
autocmd BufWinEnter * call OpenNERDTreeIfExists() " Open NERDTree on each new tab
